    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Checkout
    The program, written once against capabilities, not against IO: it needs to sequence and fail (Sync, which brings Monad and MonadError) and the two algebras.
    DashboardServer
    An HTTP API whose handler calls three downstream services in parallel, then a fourth that needs one of their answers, and combines everything with a forj comprehension over Callable.
    Euro
    Givens meant to be imported: import static forj.examples.typeclasses.Euro.*;
    Examples
     
    Generic
    The same idea, "add a and b", made more generic one step at a time.
    ImportedGivens
    An imported given beats the one next to the data type.
    Inventory<F>
    An algebra: what a program can ask of the warehouse, in any effect F.
    Ladder
    The capability ladder: each function asks for the least it needs, so it works with every effect that has at least that much.
    Live
    Interpreters in IO: the effect a real service would run in.
    Live.Bank
     
    Live.Warehouse
     
    Money
    A data type that brings its own instance: found without any import.
    Order
     
    OutOfStock
     
    Payments<F>
    An algebra: charging a customer, in any effect F.
    Plain
    Interpreters in plain Callable (Sync, but not Concurrent): e.g.
    Plain.Bank
     
    Plain.Warehouse
     
    Receipt
     
    Report
    Uses Show without passing a single instance by hand.
    RequestContext
    Per-request context that every downstream call needs.
    Resolution
    Which given gets picked.
    Resolution.Accounting
    A given in an enclosing class beats Money's own.
    Show<A>
    A type class: how to render an A as text.
    StreamMonad
    Adds Stream to forj, as a library would for its own type: import static forj.examples.StreamMonad.*; is all a caller needs.
